chapter: The Famous Door, Billy May and the Palomar fire
title: Arrangers at the Famous Door and hiding Billy May from Benny Goodman
summary: At the Famous Door Barnet employed Billy May, Andy Gibson, Billy Moore and Bud Estes, and hid May in his Park Central suite for three months so Goodman could not hire him.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And of course we went to the Famous Door shortly after that, and I sent for Billy. I said, "I want you to come in and arrange for me," you know. Oh, it was a ridiculous deal. Something like $15.00 an arrangement or something like that. And Billy was not playing in the band, he was just writing for it. He and Andy Gibson and Billy Moore, Jr., William Moore, Jr. Oh, and there was another guy by the name of Bud Estes who -- they were all writing for the band. Benny Carter contributed a couple of things. But we were -- Benny was busy elsewhere and these guys were all writing in the vein that we were exploring. Billy Moore had a tendency, and Estes, had a tendency to lean a little more toward the Lunceford approach, and of course Andy Gibson was strictly in the Duke groove, and Billy was -- he was back and forth between the two. But it made a nice lineup of arrangers, and we got some interesting scores. I had Billy in New York, and I heard that Benny Goodman -- Benny Goodman, we were playing the Famous Door, and one of the music publishers tipped me off that Benny Goodman was after Billy May, he was trying to find him. So I moved Billy. I had a suite at the Park Central Hotel, and I said, "Billy, why don't you come on and move in with me." And we had -- so Billy moved in there and we actually had him hidden. We wouldn't let him out of the room. "Oh, anything

you want, order, room service. Just keep writing." And we had him hidden from Benny. Of course at that time Benny was making so much money I couldn't have kept Billy at all. And we were successfully able to keep him away from Benny Goodman, which -- well, maybe I did him a favor.
Well, I don't think they would have gotten along very well.
Probably not. So how long did Billy live with you, then, in order to keep him?
Oh, about three months. By that time Benny had gotten somebody else to arrange for him. I don't know who it was, but he wasn't looking for an arranger anymore.
